stops.name: Kunyu Academy — Yantai
stops.detail:
Two weeks at the academy is the longest stay of the whole trip, and the rhythm does the work for you: train, eat, sleep, repeat. The mountains around Kunyushan are a national park of granite ridges and Taoist temple sites — on rest days the trails right behind the school are usually the best thing available, no transport needed.

Late November on the Shandong coast is properly cold and dry — often clear blue days around or below freezing. Training clothes that layer beat one heavy jacket: a base layer, a fleece, and a windproof shell cover everything from morning forms outside to evening classes indoors. Bring more socks than feels reasonable.

Yantai city is reachable for a day out (about an hour by car — *verify the school's usual arrangement*); most students group up and share a driver. **Cash matters here more than anywhere else on the trip:** the school itself asks for cash (it takes USD, EUR or RMB; the owner pays USD), there is no ATM near the school and the nearest town is 30 minutes away — so, per the cash plan (28 Sep 2026), no ATM is used at all: the RMB this village needs comes from changing the Exchange envelope (US$600 → ≈¥4,200) at the Beijing Daxing arrivals counter on the way in.

blocks.heading: 🚄 Getting there
items: ⚠️ **THE ACADEMY TAKES ARRIVALS ON MON/TUE/WED ONLY** (their rule, 11 Aug) — so you land in China on **Sun Nov 22**, sleep in **Muping** (Yantai), and go up the mountain on **Mon Nov 23**. The stay is **12 nights**, not 13

✅ **Nov 22 is BOOKED: Air China CA8641, PKX 15:00 → YNT T2 16:20**, $117.30 on Trip.com (PNR QEH9EM, ⏳ carried forward — verify). **Retimed by the airline 29 Sep 2026** (was CA8683, 12:35 → 13:45; the owner accepted the free change on Trip.com). It leaves from **Daxing, the airport you land at** — the only Beijing→Yantai flight that does; the rest go from PEK Capital and cost a 1.5–2 h cross-city transfer

✅ **Nov 22 bed BOOKED (28 Sep): Jinjiang Inn Select, Muping** — 锦江之星品尚酒店(烟台牟平汽车站西关夜市店), No. 460 Moushan Road · **¥164, pay CASH at the desk**, free cancellation before check-in, 18:00 arrival declared — **a later arrival, ~19:00, was requested 29 Sep** (Trip.com chat + special request) but ⏳ does not show on the order yet. Muping because the school asked for it

✅ **Dec 5 is BOOKED (28 Sep): Air China CA1560, YNT 14:55 → Beijing Capital T3 16:15**, $110.30 on Trip.com (PNR NE1K88). Air China **retimed it before it was bought** — the old 15:40 → 17:15 is dead. ⚠️ **It lands at Capital, not at Daxing.** The school books a driver to YNT (price told on arrival, per the 29 Sep voice note — the translator will help): **leave ~11:30–12:00**. The school: "December 5th is fine, you can leave. It's better before 4 p.m." — and **Saturdays do not train**

✅ **THE PICKUP (28 Sep): from 10:30 on Monday 23 Nov, in the Muping hotel lobby.** The school asked you to stay in Muping the night before — Mondays are busy, the driver also does the kitchen shopping — and **10:30 is the earliest**. It replaces the 11:00 agreed on 13 Aug ("in the hotel in muping district of yantai on 23 November 2026 at 11 am" → "**Yes,great.**"). This is the plan; the taxi is only the fallback. The city-centre question is closed: Muping it is

🚕 **The school sent its own taxi card** (13 Aug): it tells the driver to navigate to **昆嵛山武校**, use the meter, take the normal route and give a receipt — because a previous driver went the long way. It is in Key info, word for word. **~1.5h from the city**, their figure ("One and half hour around"), not the ~1h this app used to guess

🗺 **And the formal address is on file at last** (their website footer, 13 Aug): **昆嵛山少林武术学校 · 中国山东省烟台市昆嵛山自然保护区，邮编：264100** · ☎ 0086-535-4693197. ⚠️ Neither name opens **a map button** — a conservation district is an area, not a door, and nothing here has been checked against a map service. The **meeting point is the Muping hotel lobby** (28 Sep)

blocks.heading: ⚠️ Bring these or you cannot train (academy, 11 Aug · 28 Sep)
items: 🏥 **A PAPER INSURANCE CERTIFICATE** — their words (28 Sep): "Without valid insurance, you cannot join the training". Phoenix's English certificate is in hand, and **Phoenix said by phone on 28 Sep that the martial-arts training IS covered** (verbal — written confirmation and a re-issued certificate asked by email, ⏳). **PRINT IT ×2**. A policy on a phone is not what they asked for
📷 **Two passport photos** for registration (in hand) · 🩺 **a fitness report on physical paper** — the one with lead time, because it needs a doctor's appointment

💵 **THE CASH PLAN (28 Sep) — no ATM withdrawals anywhere in China.** **US$940 for the school**: $840 fee + $50 winter uniform + a **US$50 room deposit** (refundable if the room is undamaged), paid in USD from the **School envelope, US$1,000**, packed from home. **No ATM near the school** (the nearest town is 30 min away): the RMB the village needs instead comes from **changing the Exchange envelope, US$600 → ≈¥4,200, at the Beijing Daxing arrivals counter on Nov 22**. Bank transfers are discouraged. ✅ **The US$100 already paid was a one-time APPLICATION FEE — NOT part of the $840**

💊 **Common medicine** — cold, muscle soreness. ⚠️ But check it against the customs rule: **codeine and tramadol count as narcotics, and "-D" cold medicines (pseudoephedrine) are controlled**. They do not know that; you do

📱 **Message them the day you land.** ⚠️ They point out a **VPN is needed for WhatsApp** in China. Since the **April 2026 crackdown made most consumer VPNs unreliable** (chinavpns.com · startchinatravel.com · simology.io, Sept 2026 guides), **plan A is a Hong Kong-routed roaming travel eSIM** (APN of the cmhk type), installed and TESTED before you fly — the VPN is the backup. Without one of them the channel for telling them you arrived is the one that is blocked

🛂 **Police (PSB) registration — THE SCHOOL DOES IT** (28 Sep): "you're going to meet school Jennifer and she will do all for you and register in local government and police station". Hand over the passport; there is nothing else to do. (The rule: a foreigner staying anywhere that is not a hotel is registered within 24 h, by the host — en.nia.gov.cn · china-briefing.com)

📜 **School rules** (28 Sep): no romantic or intimate relationships during the stay; no drugs, controlled substances, weapons or anything prohibited under Chinese law — immediate expulsion, and the police

✅ **The private-room question is closed, by decision rather than by answer** — the owner, 13 Aug: "i dont care about the private room". The base shared room it is, and **no room surcharge is expected on top of the $940**

blocks.heading: 📅 How their week lands on yours
items: 🧹 **Cleaning duty every Mon/Wed/Fri morning**, before classes — staff and students together, part of the timetable rather than an extra. Six of them fall inside the stay: **Nov 23, 25, 27, 30 and Dec 2, 4**

☀️ **Two days off, not one: Sat Nov 28 and Sun Nov 29.** No training on Saturdays or Sundays (the school, 28 Sep). Nov 28 has one optional thing — a **free 1–2 h class with a shifu**, the school's gift, accepted (time ⏳). Nov 29 carries one job: the **20:00 Forbidden City ticket release** (the gear run moved to the Nov 22 arrival night)
✅ **The Saturdays are answered (28 Sep): no training on Saturdays or Sundays.** Dec 5 — the day you fly to Beijing — cuts nothing short, and the school is happy for you to leave "before 4 p.m."

✅ **The first-day question is answered: they collect you from the Muping hotel lobby, from 10:30 on Monday Nov 23** (28 Sep; it was 11:00 on 13 Aug). You no longer go up the mountain alone to an address nobody had given you — the address is on file, and the Nov 22 bed is booked in Muping

options.heading: ⭐ Our picks
items: ⭐ **The park behind the school** — Kunyu Mountain National Forest Park is granite ridges, pine and old Taoist temple sites, and the trails start where the academy ends. The default rest-day outing, no transport needed *(verify the current gate fee and which trails are open in winter)*
⭐ **One full Yantai day** — Yantai Hill Park, the Suochengli lanes and a bowl of seafood noodles all sit within a walk of each other. Go once, do it properly, come back tired
⭐ **Penglai**, about an hour north — the sea-cliff pavilion and the old sea wall, near-empty in December. The one big sight worth leaving the school for
⭐ **A bathhouse or foot-massage afternoon** on a Sunday — cheap, hot, and exactly what a fortnight of training asks for. Ask the school where students go *(verify locally)*
⭐ **Sort the boring things in the first two days** — laundry, the village shop, how you get a taxi. It decides how comfortable the other twelve feel

options.heading: ➕ More options
items: **Yangma Island** (养马岛) — a low coastal loop east of Muping, close to the academy; oyster shacks, empty beaches, hard wind
**Zhifu Island** (芝罘岛) — the headland north of Yantai with a cliff path and a small fishing harbour; almost nobody in winter
**Yantai Museum**, in the old Fujian Guild Hall — carved timber and sea-goddess halls, indoors and warm *(verify opening days)*
**Weihai** for a day, about an hour by train — the seafront park, the Happiness Gate and the Liugong Island ferry *(verify winter ferry times before going)*
**A hot spring** — the Kunyushan and Muping area has several resort spring pools; a plausible reward on a rest day *(verify which are open and how to reach them)*
**A fish-market lunch in Yantai** — pick the catch, they cook it next door, you pay by weight *(verify locally; take cash)*
Foggy or wet day: stay in and train forms in the hall. The ridge is exposed and the granite gets slick — this is the one place where the boring choice is the right one
Evenings: the village has a shop and not much else. Download films, books and offline maps before you fly — there is nothing to buy locally and the VPN is not guaranteed

options.heading: 🍜 Where to eat
items: ⭐ **Muping 牟平, ~30 minutes** — the nearest real town, where students go at weekends: a market street, supermarkets, malls. **Muping is known for its 烧烤 barbecue**, and that is the right reward after a training week
⭐ **三和园 Sanhe Yuan, Chaoyang Food Street, Yantai** — the city's signature **鲅鱼饺子 mackerel dumplings**. The one unmissable dish here
⭐ **福山大面 Fushan hand-pulled noodles** — a 200-year tradition with a seafood soup topping; Fushan is the birthplace of the style
**Chaoyang Food Street** generally — Shandong seafood: sea cucumber with scallions, razor clams, prawns
**烟台焖子 Yantai menzi** — fried bean jelly with shrimp paste, the local street snack
**Penglai 小面** if the Penglai Pavilion day trip happens
**Happiness Night Market** for cheap volume
⭐ **Yantai apples.** You arrive in apple season in the region famous for them — buy them by the bag
The village around the school has a couple of good restaurants, and students rate the food near the academy well *(verify locally — this is student report, not a named address)*

stops.name: Beijing
stops.detail:
The Palace Museum (Forbidden City) is the one thing in Beijing you cannot improvise: tickets are released **seven days ahead** and sell out fast, it is **closed on Mondays**, and entry is tied to your passport — book with the same French passport you travel on *(verify the current booking window on the official WeChat/web channel when you book)*. Go early: the light on snow-dusted roofs before the crowds arrive is the picture everyone chases. Climb Jingshan hill just north afterwards for the view over the whole golden-roofed city — best in the last hour before sunset.

For the Great Wall, **Mutianyu** is the first-timer's right answer in winter: further than Badaling but far quieter, with a cable car up and a toboggan run down. Watch the forecast — a clear day after wind is gold; ice can close sections *(verify conditions the day before)*.

December in Beijing is dry, bright and biting — usually −5 to a few degrees. The wind matters more than the number: a real hat and gloves change the whole day. Evenings belong to the hutongs around Gulou: small restaurants, warm noodle shops, and Peking duck that needs no reservation at lunch but often does at dinner.

**Dec 7–9:** Blossom House Prince Kung's Mansion · Beijing Houhai — **booked and PREPAID, $299.56** (Trip.com), breakfast for 1 · **heating confirmed before booking** · **free cancellation to 23:00 on Dec 4**, non-refundable after (both off the confirmation email, read 27 Sep) · 北京西城区德内大街羊房胡同9号 · the 9.9-from-969-reviews and 900 m-to-the-Drum-Tower claims were researched under the property's older, plainer name — verify · closest base to Qinghe, where you leave from on Dec 9

dayRows.text: **Great Wall wild-wall trek** — 6:30 pickup at **Four Points Sanlitun** (checked out, **backpack rides in the driver's trunk all day**) → Jinshanling → Tower 22 (in-gate; Wohushan extension = booking-time call), ~7km / 3.5–5h, heading down by ~13:30, out the East Gate before 15:00 → driver drops you + bag at **Blossom House, Houhai** ~17:30 → deep tuina near Gulou (~¥220) → early sleep

dayRows.label: Dec 8 Tue
dayRows.text: 🧖 **Pressure-off spa day** — clinical morning at **护国寺中医医院 骨伤科** (Huguosi TCM Hospital, outpatient campus 航空胡同42号, ☎ 56895700, a 10–15 min walk from Blossom House — bone-setting is one of its two 国家级重点专科 and the institutional home of 宫廷正骨, the Qing court lineage. Weekdays 8:00–11:30 and 13:00–16:30, so a morning X-ray is not against a cutoff; expect them to want one before they manipulate anything, and say you ski on Thursday. ~¥150–600 — verify, the hospital publishes no price list) → all-day hot springs at Jiuhua Resort (Xiaotangshan, ~1h north; ¥138 day pass, 70+ pools; quieter alternative: Chunhuiyuan 春晖园) · early night. Heat after bodywork, legs fresh for skiing.

options.heading: ⭐ Our picks

⭐ **Gulou at opening time** — climb the Drum or Bell Tower for the hutong rooftops, then eat your way south through Baochao and Doujiao hutongs
⭐ **The National Museum on Tiananmen Square** — free, enormous and warm; the grey-day answer that never disappoints *(verify the current booking rule — passport entry, usually reserved in advance)*
⭐ **Nanluoguxiang's side lanes, not its main drag** — the parallel hutongs east and west are where the quiet courtyard bars are

items: **Beijing Ancient Observatory** — Ming and Qing bronze instruments on a surviving city-wall tower, ten minutes from Jianguomen
**Ming Tombs and the Sacred Way** — the tree-lined spirit road with its stone animals; often combined with a Great Wall day and best in bare winter light
**Panjiayuan antique market** — the real version happens on weekend mornings; bargaining expected *(verify the weekday hours, most good stalls are Sat–Sun)*
**Sanlitun Taikoo Li** in the evening — modern Beijing, international food, and the district your first hotel is in
**Capital Museum** — the city's own story, quieter than the national one and just as warm *(verify booking)*
**Wangfujing** for the church, the bookshop street and an indoor hour when the wind is unbearable
Foggy or freezing alternate: the **Palace Museum's own galleries** — ceramics, clocks and the treasure halls are all indoors and included in the ticket
**Caochangdi or Songzhuang** if 798 leaves you wanting more art *(verify what is open — many spaces shut for winter)*

options.heading: 🍜 Where to eat
items: ⭐ **四季民福 Siji Minfu, Donghuamen branch** — the Peking duck locals name, five minutes from the Forbidden City's east exit. Whole duck **¥168–228**, no tourist surcharge. Ask for a window table: it looks at the moat and the corner tower. **Book — weekend waits run 90 minutes**

⭐ **南门涮肉 Nanmen Hotpot** — copper-pot instant-boiled mutton over charcoal, nothing in the broth but scallion and ginger. *The* Beijing winter meal. The original is by the Temple of Heaven's south gate, a long way from Houhai *(verify a nearer branch)*. Same tradition: **东来顺 Donglaishun**, **一条龙 Yitiaolong**

⭐ **姚记炒肝 Yaoji Chaoguan, 311 Gulou Dongdajie** — one of the last places doing the real Beijing breakfast stew, plus baozi and **炸酱面 zhajiangmian**. Cheap, hot, minutes from Blossom House. A breakfast place first *(verify evening hours)*
**大董 Da Dong** — the modern duck, crispest skin in the city, ¥400–600pp with drinks. The splurge version
**利群 Liqun** — 1864, down a crumbling alley south of Tiananmen; the atmospheric one rather than the best one
**Toast at The Orchid**, 65 Baochao Hutong — roof terrace with Drum Tower views when you want a break from Chinese food
**Carry your own food on Dec 7.** There is nothing reliable on the Jinshanling wall in December and no signal to summon any — buy in Sanlitun the night before, and **two litres of water minimum**

stops.name: Chongli — first-time ski
stops.detail:
Chongli is China's Olympic ski country — high, cold and reliably snowy from late November. For a first time on skis, book a **lesson for the first morning** rather than the second day: one hour of basics saves two days of frustration. English-speaking instructors exist at the bigger resorts but are limited — reserve ahead *(verify availability when booking)*.

Rental covers skis, boots and helmet; it usually does **not** include goggles, gloves or a face covering, and at −15°C on a lift all three are non-negotiable. Buy hand warmers at any convenience store and put one in each boot at lunch.

Pace the first day: the beginner zones are wide and forgiving, and the magic-carpet lifts mean no chairlift stress until you want it. Drink more water than you think you need — the air is extremely dry — and stop while your legs still feel good; almost every first-day injury happens on the "one last run".

stops.name: Zhangjiajie
stops.whenLabel: Fri Dec 11 → Mon Dec 14 · 2n park + 1n city
stops.detail:
The sandstone pillars of Wulingyuan are what *Avatar* borrowed, and December is the quiet season: thin crowds, low prices, and fog that either steals the view or makes it — often both in one day. Build the days flexible: if the morning is socked in, do the lower valley (Golden Whip Stream) and save the viewpoints for the first clearing.

The park ticket covers multiple days *(verify the current validity when buying)*; inside, the **Bailong glass elevator** and the cable cars are the knees-saving way up — queues that are brutal in summer are short in December, but wind can pause them, so never plan the last descent tight. Tianzi Mountain and Yuanjiajie hold the classic pillar panoramas.

Winter practicalities: the stone stairs stay damp and slick under fog — shoes with real grip matter more than warmth. Temperatures hover around 0–8°C; the valley floor is milder than the tops. Monkeys near the stream are charming and will unzip your bag — keep food buried.

stops.name: Chongqing
stops.detail:
Chongqing is the mountain megacity — 8D streets where a "ground floor" door can open onto a rooftop. Don't fight it with maps too much; the city rewards wandering between levels.

**Hongyadong** at night is the postcard: a cliff of stacked wooden pavilions in lantern light. Go after dark (lights typically until late evening — *verify locally*), see it once from across the river for the full face, then once inside for the food floors. The **Yangtze River cableway** nearby is a short ride with the best skyline angle — the queue moves faster than it looks in December.

Hotpot is the city religion, and Chongqing spice is a different sport: 微辣 ("wei la", mild) is already serious — order the split pot (鸳鸯锅) with a clear side without shame; every table around you will understand. Numbing (麻) from Sichuan pepper is normal and passes. December is mild here (8–12°C), often misty — the haze actually flatters the neon.

stops.name: Lijiang
stops.detail:
Lijiang old town sits at **2,400 m** — the first altitude of the trip. Take the first evening slow: walk the canals, eat, sleep well; headaches usually come from rushing and dehydration, not the altitude itself.

The old town is a maze on purpose. Getting lost is the activity; the Naxi courtyard houses, water channels and Sifang square are best before 9am, before the day-trip crowds, and again after dark when the lanterns come on. There is a small old-town maintenance fee collected at guesthouses or gates *(verify the current amount)*.

**Jade Dragon Snow Mountain** is the big day out: in December the peak is properly snowbound and the air is thin — the Glacier Park cable car tops out above 4,500 m. Book the cable car slot in advance (it caps daily numbers — *verify how your guesthouse books it, they all do it routinely*), move slowly up top, and skip the canned oxygen theatrics unless you actually feel bad. The Blue Moon Valley lakes below the mountain keep their unreal color in winter and cost far less effort.

stops.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge
stops.detail:
Tiger Leaping Gorge is one of the deepest gorges on earth — the Jinsha (upper Yangtze) thundering between Jade Dragon and Haba Snow Mountains. December is the **dry season: stable trails, clear views**, cold mornings and pleasant walking by mid-day.

With one night, the classic move is the **high trail** as far as the guesthouses (Naxi Family, Tea Horse, Halfway) rather than racing the whole traverse: start early, take the 28 Bends slowly — it's the only genuinely hard hour — and let the gorge do the rest. The views from the Halfway terraces at sunset justify the entire detour. The low road and the riverside Tiger Leaping Stone are a separate short visit, reachable by shuttle from the trailhead towns *(verify times locally — they thin out in winter)*.

Real shoes, water, sun cream (the UV at this altitude is stronger than the temperature suggests), and a headlamp just in case. Guesthouses stay open in December but evenings are cold — ask for the extra blanket before you need it.

blocks.heading: 🥾 The hike
items: Day 1 (Dec 18): Qiaotou → 28 Bends → **Halfway Guesthouse** (~5–6h) · lunch stop: **Tea Horse Guesthouse** terrace just past the Bends
Day 2 (Dec 19): high trail → Tina's (~3–4h) → shared car toward Dali, stopping at Jane's for the bag (eve)
The Middle Rock valley-floor descent (Sky Ladder) is currently closed — the **high trail is the trek**

⚠️ **2026 was a bad year on the gorge road**: mudslide 23–24 Jul, rockfall 30 Jul, closure 31 Jul, reopened ~3 Aug, a minor rockfall 1 Sep, "operating normally" 2 Sep (the scenic area is administered from Shangri-La; which sections were hit is unclear). ¥65 entry and the **public bus, Lijiang → Qiaotou (~08:00, verify)** are the way in — Yue Tu's private car and bag transfer were declined 27 Sep, and the inn has no contact for Tina's Inn either. **On Dec 17 ask Yue Tu for the trail status**

🎒 **Bag plan — Option B, decided 27 Sep 2026:** the bag rides the public bus to Qiaotou with you and waits in the luggage room at **Jane's Guesthouse** (≈¥5, non-guests) while you hike with a day pack; the Dec 19 shared car to Dali stops at Jane's to collect it. Tina's own bus is the backup (Option A), contact unknown

🔁 **The fallback, decided in advance:** if you are not at Tea Horse by **~15:00**, sleep there instead of pushing on to Halfway · if the trail is **closed or icy**, take a minibus along the gorge road to **Tina's** and sleep there · the bag still waits at Jane's either way · **Dec 19 is unchanged** either way

stops.name: Dali
stops.detail:
Dali is the exhale after the gorge: a walled old town between the **Cangshan range** and **Erhai lake**, at a gentler 1,900 m. In December the light is sharp and golden and the famous Xiaguan wind is real — sunny afternoons, cold gusts, perfect walking weather in layers.

With one night, keep it simple: the **Three Pagodas** with the mountains behind them are the signature view (the reflection pond at the back of the complex is the photo), then the old town's gates and the food street as the lanterns come on. If there's a spare hour, any stretch of the Erhai lakeside path delivers — wintering birds included.

Dali baba (stuffed flatbread) and a pot of local pu'er in a courtyard teahouse cover lunch properly. Rose-petal pastries are everywhere and travel well as small gifts.

stops.detail:
Kunming is the safety night before the exit flight — but it hides a genuinely wonderful December ritual: every winter, thousands of **red-billed gulls from Siberia** descend on the city, and **Green Lake (Cuihu)** turns into a swirling white spectacle. They arrive in November and stay through the winter, so your date lands exactly in the window. An hour at the lake at golden hour, a bag of bread you probably shouldn't buy but will, and the trip gets one last unplanned highlight.

Around the lake, Wenlin Street and the university quarter do relaxed cafés and Yunnan coffee — the province grows most of China's beans, and it's very good.

Keep the evening honest: this night exists to make the visa deadline unmissable. Pack for the morning before going out, confirm the airport transfer time, and treat everything else as bonus.

stops.name: Hong Kong — Christmas Finale
stops.detail:
Hong Kong at Christmas is the finale working in your favor: the whole city dresses up — harbour-front light shows, giant decorations in the malls and squares, and mild 15–20°C days that feel tropical after the north. **WinterFest** installations cluster around Tsim Sha Tsui and Central *(check that year's locations when you arrive)*.

The essentials still win: the **Star Ferry** at dusk for pennies, the **Peak** just after sunset when the lights come on (take the bus up if the tram queue is silly), and the Temple Street night market for the noise of it. Christmas Eve and Christmas Day evenings are the two densest crowds of the year around the harbour — go early or pick a bar window.

Get an **Octopus card** in the first hour (it works on everything, including many shops) — and note Hong Kong is outside the mainland's networks: your VPN is unnecessary here and normal SIM/eSIM data just works. If legs allow one hike, **Dragon's Back** is a two-hour ridge walk with sea views that ends at a beach bus stop — a strange and perfect thing to do at Christmas.

checklists.title: Before you fly
checklists.note: All of this must work BEFORE landing.

items.label: **Alipay** — link the foreign card, test a real charge before flying. Everything in China is QR. In 2026 foreign cards work with limits of roughly US$5,000 per payment.
**WeChat Pay** — same (fee-free under ¥200 in 2026); also the platform for ticket mini-programs — Forbidden City 故宫博物院, and Jade Dragon's 玉龙雪山服务 + 丽江旅游集团.

**NordVPN — the BACKUP** since the April 2026 crackdown made most consumer VPNs unreliable in China — installed, logged in, set to **NordWhisper / obfuscated**, a few servers favorited. Default NordLynx is blocked. nordvpn.com is unreachable inside China, so this must be done BEFORE landing.

**Travel eSIM — PLAN A**: Hong Kong-routed roaming (APN of the cmhk type), ~30 days mainland + ~5 days HK/Macau, activate-before date after Nov 22 — bought early Nov, installed and TESTED before Nov 21. Roaming data bypasses the firewall.
**Home SIM stays active with roaming SMS** — Alipay, WeChat, 12306 and bank 3-D Secure all verify by SMS. Enable bank app-push as backup.
**CDAC** — China Digital Arrival Card, file online before the Nov 21 flight.
**12306** — register + verify on the passport by early Nov (3–5 day manual review).
**AMap Global** — Google Maps' China data is offset even on VPN; AMap gives exact metro exit numbers.
**DiDi** — or the mini-program inside Alipay/WeChat. In-app driver chat auto-translates.
**Trip.com app** — all five domestic flights live in "My Bookings".

infoCards.heading: Visa — the one unforgivable number
items: French passport: **30 days visa-free**, policy valid through Dec 31 2026 (hk.ocmfa.gov.cn · gov.cn, Nov 2025 — re-checked 27 Sep 2026).
The count starts **the day AFTER entry** (embassy-verified). Entry Nov 22 → day 1 is Nov 23.
**Legal deadline: Dec 22, 24:00.** Planned exit Dec 21 = day 29, a 1-day buffer.
Hong Kong is separate and does not count against it. A mainland re-entry from HK starts a fresh visa-free window (and needs a new CDAC).
No extensions. Overstay ≤10 days = warning; ¥500/day from day 11. Still: do not let the Dec 21 flight slip.

infoCards.heading: The 20 kg rule
items: ⚠️ **FIVE domestic flights now, not three — and the cap starts on DAY ONE.** Adding the Yantai pair (Nov 22 out, Dec 5 back) means the 20 kg limit bites from **Nov 22**, three weeks earlier than this card used to imply. Etihad brings you in on 40 kg; the very next flight halves it.
All the domestic legs cap checked baggage at **20 kg** (CA1560 +5 kg cabin, CA8609 +5 kg cabin, 3U8011 +8 kg cabin).

🥋 **The squeeze is the gear run.** You buy training kit, thermals and fleece in Yantai on **Nov 22** — and all of it flies out with you on **Dec 5 under 20 kg**. Weigh the bag at the academy, not at the YNT counter.
Etihad allows 40 kg — so the bag can only grow again after Hong Kong (MU733 Business is 2 × 32 kg).
Keep the Traker 90 half-empty leaving home; shed worn-out training kit as you go.

infoCards.heading: Power banks
items: Domestic China flights **ban power banks without a clear 3C logo** — and any recalled/faulty ones.
Check yours before Nov 21; buy a 3C-marked one in Yantai if in doubt.

infoCards.heading: Airport traps
items: **Dec 11 departs Daxing (PKX), NOT Capital (PEK)** — the same airport you land at on Nov 22. It used to be Capital: Air China moved the original CA1953 to 07:45, and on 27 Sep 2026 the booking was changed free onto **CA8609**. Any older note that sends Dec 11 to PEK is out of date.
CA8609 · PKX 18:15 → Zhangjiajie 20:30. Zhangjiajie is fog-prone. Fallbacks if it is cancelled: the morning nonstops (CA1953, now 07:45 from PEK *verify* · CA9659) · Changsha + HSR.
**Dec 5 lands at Capital (PEK) T3, NOT at Daxing** — CA1560, YNT 14:55 → PEK 16:15, booked 28 Sep. Air China had already moved it from 15:40 → 17:15 before it was bought.
Winter schedules firm up in autumn — re-verify all internal flight times Sept–Oct.

infoCards.heading: Kunyu arrival
items: **They collect you from the Muping hotel lobby, from 10:30 on Monday 23 Nov** — the school, 28 Sep: stay in Muping the night before (Mondays are busy), earliest pickup 10:30. It replaces the 11:00 agreed on 13 Aug. The Nov 22 bed is booked there: Jinjiang Inn Select, Muping — **¥164 in cash at the desk**.

Fallback if the pickup fails: **~1.5h taxi** (the school's own figure), ~$50 — and **the school's own driver card is the one to hand over**: it navigates to 昆嵛山武校 and asks for the meter, the normal route and a receipt. It carries **no map button** on purpose; hand it over, do not follow a pin. Formal address on the academy's card in Stays: 昆嵛山少林武术学校, 昆嵛山自然保护区, 烟台 264100.

**$940 in cash on arrival, from the School envelope (US$1,000)** — USD: $840 stay + $50 winter uniform + $50 refundable room-keeping. ✅ **The $100 already sent was a one-time application fee, NOT part of the $840** (28 Sep). **No ATM near the school, and no ATM anywhere on this trip** (the cash plan, 28 Sep): the village's RMB comes from the Exchange envelope, changed at Beijing Daxing on Nov 22. No room surcharge: the private room was dropped on 13 Aug.

Mandatory, in the school's words — missing any one "is not allowed": the cash, **a PAPER insurance certificate** ("Without valid insurance, you cannot join the training" — Phoenix confirmed the martial-arts cover by phone, 28 Sep; **print ×2**), and **two passport photos**. **PSB registration: the school does it** — Jennifer registers you with the local police; hand over the passport.

**No training on Saturdays or Sundays.** Sat Nov 28: a free 1–2 h class with a shifu, the school's gift (accepted, time ⏳). School rules: no romantic or intimate relationships during the stay; no drugs, controlled substances or weapons — expulsion, and the police.

infoCards.heading: Dec 16 — the late arrival
items: Chongqing → Lijiang is an **evening flight landing ~22:00**.
The Naxi Ancient Music concert moved to **Dec 17**.

**The late arrival is approved** — Yue Tu Inn accepted a 22:00–23:00 window when the bed was booked, and its 24-hour front desk is confirmed on the booking page. ☎ +86 151 5325 4963. Lijiang is 2,400m — go easy that night.
The inn offered an airport pickup for 80 and you accepted on 27 Sep with this flight — ⏳ not confirmed yet; a taxi is the fallback. WeChat yanglei400371.

infoCards.heading: Trains
items: Your **passport IS the ticket** — use the manual channel (人工通道), arrive ~45 min early; gates close 4–5 min before departure.
Booking opens on a 15-day window; the sale hour varies by station (check 起售时间 in the 12306 app).
"Dali" on train apps = the station in Xiaguan, ~30–45 min from the old town *verify*.
Dec 20 arrives **Kunming Station 昆明站** (central) by plan, **Kunming South** as the fallback. The station in Xiaguan is DALI's, not Kunming's.

infoCards.heading: Hotels & registration
items: Only PSB-linked hotels can legally host foreigners — filter **"accepts foreign guests"** and keep every registration slip.
Non-hotel stays (the academy) = **registered with the PSB within 24 h**, by the host or in person (en.nia.gov.cn · china-briefing.com). At Kunyu **the school does it** (28 Sep).

infoCards.heading: Money
items: Alipay + WeChat Pay with a foreign card — everything is QR. In 2026 foreign cards take limits of roughly **US$5,000 per payment**, and WeChat Pay charges **no fee under ¥200**.

🏧 **No ATM withdrawals anywhere in China, by decision (28 Sep)** — dollars are brought from home and exchanged once: **US$600 → ≈¥4,200 at the Beijing Daxing arrivals counter, Nov 22** (passport, keep the receipt). It covers **¥164 Muping** (cash at the desk) · **~¥1,000** small spending near the school (no ATM there; nearest town 30 min) · **~¥1,500** kept for **Tiger Leaping Gorge, Dec 18–19, cash only** (Qiaotou ATMs are China-cards-only anyway) · **~¥500** elsewhere · the rest is margin.

The school wants **US$940 in cash, USD**, from the **School envelope (US$1,000)** on Nov 23; the Muping hotel takes its **¥164** in cash from the Nov 22 exchange. Everything else — hotels, restaurants, trains, taxis, tickets — is **card, through Alipay / WeChat Pay**.
**Hong Kong, Dec 21:** change **~US$50 → HKD** at HKG airport for cash-only spots (Yat Lok); card / Octopus for the rest.
**Before leaving:** tell the bank about China + Hong Kong (Nov 21 – Dec 27), and pack two cards in two separate places.
Hong Kong uses HKD + cards; carry some cash for the old-school food spots.

**The Trip.com gift card is spent and the question is closed** (12 Aug) — $52.96 of it went on Blossom House, which is prepaid in full; every pay-at-hotel figure in this app is the platform's own, so nothing at a desk is overstated.

infoCards.heading: Medication
items: Codeine and tramadol count as narcotics; "-D" cold medicines (pseudoephedrine) are controlled.
Carry a doctor's letter and keep everything in original packaging.

infoCards.heading: Tickets & apps
items: Big sights sell via real-name **WeChat mini-programs at ~20:00, 7 days ahead** — set an alarm per city.
Forbidden City: mini-program 故宫博物院, winter ¥40, passport = ticket.
SF Express forwards suitcases hotel-to-hotel (~¥30–80 overnight between big cities); stations have left-luggage counters (passport needed).

infoCards.heading: Internet in China
items: Google, Gmail web and most CDNs are blocked. **This app works fully offline** — nothing in it needs the network except the "Find email" buttons.

**Plan A is a Hong Kong-routed travel eSIM** (APN of the cmhk type) — it roams around the firewall. The April 2026 crackdown made most consumer VPNs unreliable in China (chinavpns.com · startchinatravel.com · simology.io, Sept 2026 guides).
NordVPN is the **backup**, on an **obfuscated protocol (NordWhisper)**, set up before landing.
No VPN needed in Hong Kong.

infoCards.heading: The VPN, specifically
items: nordvpn.com is **blocked inside China** — you cannot install or fix it once you land. Before Nov 21: install NordVPN, log in, switch the protocol to **NordWhisper / obfuscated** (the default NordLynx is blocked), favorite a few servers, and confirm it actually connects.

**It is the BACKUP now, not plan A.** The April 2026 crackdown made most consumer VPNs unreliable in mainland China (chinavpns.com · startchinatravel.com · simology.io, Sept 2026 guides). Plan A is a **Hong Kong-routed travel eSIM** (APN of the cmhk type), bought early November and tested before Nov 21 — see the eSIM task.
